test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beat around the bush.

options.text: To avoid talking about what is important.

solution: The correct answer is **Option 3)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Beat around the bush"** means to avoid talking about what is important. (महत्वपूर्ण बात से बचना) • **Example: **Stop **beating around the bush** and tell me what you really think. • **Explanation:** The idiom suggests that instead of addressing the main issue directly, someone is avoiding it or talking about irrelevant things. (मुख्य मुद्दे को संबोधित करने के बजाय, कोई व्यक्ति इससे बच रहा है या अप्रासंगिक चीजों के बारे में बात कर रहा है) • **Example: **When asked about the company's financial problems, the CEO** beat around the bush **and didn't provide a clear answer. Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is **'To avoid talking about what is important.'** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: To go around the bush** (झाड़ी के चारों ओर जाना): This is a literal interpretation and does not convey the idiomatic meaning. • **Example:** They decided** to go around the bush** to reach the other side. • **Option 2: To live around the bush** (झाड़ी के चारों ओर रहना): This does not convey the idiomatic meaning either. • **Example: **Many people **live around the bush **in rural areas. • **Option 4: To talk about something important** (महत्वपूर्ण बात के बारे में बात करना): This is the opposite of the idiomatic meaning. • **Example:** Let's **talk about something important l**ike our future plans. 342:Tafa, The correct answer is **Option 1)**
